description: How human arm signals become SO-ARM101 joint targets. robot_ticks = home + sign * gain * (human - human_at_home) * 4096/360, clamped to the motor limits minus margin_ticks. 'verified' means the direction was checked on the physical arm. Each signal is low-pass filtered with smooth_s before mapping, because the motors cap at ~32 deg/s.

shoulder_pan.source: camera shoulder_pan (0 deg = upper arm forward, +90 = out to your side)
shoulder_pan.note: Undefined while the upper arm is near vertical; the robot holds its last pan there.

shoulder_lift.source: camera shoulder_lift (0 deg hanging, 180 straight up)
shoulder_lift.note: Larger ticks tilt the arm forward/down from straight up (checked on the arm). Gain 0.55 squeezes your 180 deg (hanging to straight up) into the robot's ~100 deg forward range, since it cannot point down through the table.

elbow_flex.note: Home is straight, 217 ticks above the minimum, so bending must increase ticks.

wrist_flex.note: The camera gives bend size but not up vs down, so this only bends one way.

wrist_roll.source: band roll relative to its median during the 'rest' step
wrist_roll.note: Experimental: band roll also picks up whole-arm tilt, so it is scaled down by half.

gripper.source: EMG clench strength: 0 at the 'rest' step level, 1 at the 'sync' clench peak
gripper.note: gain is ticks at full clench. The leader arm has a handle, not a claw.
